newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Uralsvyazinform placed shares in London.
newsitem.headline: Uralsvyazinform placed shares in London.

text.p: Russian regional telecom AO Uralsvyazinform sold one percent of its shares through the London Stock Exchange in January and plans a similar private placement in the U.S., the company's chief executive said on Tuesday.
Vladimir Rybakin told Reuters the unlisted shares had been sold through Williams de Broe brokerage, which won a tender to place the shares.
He said the U.S. Securities Exchange Commission (SEC) was reviewing a plan by the company, based in the southern Urals city of Perm, to issue level-one American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
He said Brunswick Brokerage would make another private placement, the size of which was not yet determined, in the U.S.
Uralsvyazinform's economics director Alexander Vokhmin said U.S. investors had been the major buyers of the shares placed in London.
Rybakin said the SEC was holding talks with The Bank of New York, the likely depository for the Uralsvyazinform ADRs.
"We are generally interested in selling shares of our company to Western investors," he said. "But first we must issue an ADR in order to raise the share price."
He said the shares were currently trading at $0.038-$0.040 in London.

But Rybakin said the SEC could put the ADR project, planned to represent 10 percent of company stock, on hold due to uncertainty about Russian telecom holding company Svyazinvest, which owns controlling shares in Uralsvyazinform.
Russia has said it will sell 25 percent of Svyazinvest to foreign portfolio investors and 24 percent to Russian investors.

Svyazinvest has blocked a Uralsvyazinform plan to issue new shares equal to 10 percent of company equity. Uralsvyazinform planned to sell a controlling share in the new issue to Svyazinvest at the average auction price but the company declined.
Svyazinvest owns 51 percent, Uralsvyazinform itself owns 12 percent, employees 28.8 percent and Crawford Holdings three percent.
Its shares are traded on the RTS-2 system in Russia, and were quoted late on Tuesday at $0.048/$0.052.
